question: What core responsibility does a registered nurse retain after delegating a task?

options.B: Direct execution of all bedside procedures
options.C: Financial liability for facility equipment use
options.D: Professional accountability for the patient outcome

explanation: Even when a task is transferred to another worker, the registered nurse keeps ultimate accountability for the quality of care provided. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why is delegation necessary in busy clinical environments?

options.A: It optimizes the utilization of available nursing manpower
options.B: It reduces the need for patient assessments by nurses
options.C: It shifts all legal blame entirely to support staff
options.D: It eliminates the requirement for nurse supervision

explanation: Task sharing helps distribute workloads so that professional nurses can focus on complex clinical decisions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h1)

question: Which of the Five Rights involves confirming that a staff member has the correct training?
explanation: The right person principle requires checking that the individual receiving the assignment is actually competent to perform it. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h2)

question: A nurse asks a ward attendant to check vital signs on an unstable patient. Which right is violated here?
explanation: An unstable patient creates a situation where standard delegated tasks are unsafe to perform, violating the right circumstance. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary duty of the delegatee after accepting a task?

options.A: Reassign the duty to another junior worker
options.B: Document the care plan adjustments in the chart
options.D: Report abnormal findings promptly to the nurse

explanation: The delegatee must communicate any unexpected changes or abnormal findings back to the delegating nurse immediately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h3)

question: A junior nursing assistant refuses a delegated task because it falls outside their training. How should this be handled?

options.A: Perform the task yourself without addressing the employee
options.B: Respect the refusal and assign a task within their scope
options.C: Force the worker to complete the procedure under supervision
options.D: Report the staff member for insubordination to management

explanation: Staff members have a duty to decline tasks that exceed their legal and educational scope of practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h3)

question: A patient with fluctuating vital signs is admitted to the ward. Why should delegation be limited in this case?

options.A: Auxiliary staff members charge higher fees for unstable patients
options.B: The unpredictable clinical condition requires continuous professional assessment
options.C: Unstable patients always prefer care from senior doctors
options.D: Hospital policies forbid any nurse from taking breaks

explanation: Unpredictable health states demand the critical thinking and advanced skills of a registered nurse rather than auxiliary workers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which factor is most critical when evaluating environmental stability before delegating?

options.A: Availability of emergency equipment and adequate staffing levels
options.B: Proximity of the administrative offices to the patient
options.C: The personal friendship between the nurse and delegatee
options.D: The physical color scheme of the hospital ward

explanation: A safe environment requires proper staffing and functional equipment to handle potential complications arising from patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: A nurse insists on performing every basic bed bath because no one else can do it right. What barrier is this nurse demonstrating?

options.B: Proper adherence to the five rights

explanation: Unwillingness to let go of simple tasks due to mistrust of others hinders efficient workload distribution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective delegation?

options.B: Fear of liability by the registered nurse
options.C: Poor communication channels on the ward
options.D: Lack of role clarity among junior workers

explanation: Having enough competent staff actually facilitates delegation rather than serving as a barrier to it. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h5)

question: Who holds the legal accountability when a delegated task goes wrong due to poor nurse assessment?

options.A: The hospital cleaner who witnessed the procedure
options.B: The junior staff member who executed the task
options.C: The pharmaceutical company supplying the ward
options.D: The registered nurse who made the delegation decision

explanation: The professional nurse remains legally accountable for evaluating the patient and deciding whether delegation is appropriate in the first place. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of active supervision during a delegated procedure?

options.A: To ensure compliance with clinical standards and offer guidance
options.B: To minimize the paperwork required for the shift
options.C: To replace the need for any initial patient assessment
options.D: To find fault and punish staff for minor mistakes

explanation: Supervision helps catch errors early, provides mentorship, and ensures the patient receives safe, quality care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h6)
